text:
aya: Heads up — started a short probe on the multi-GPU tensor+pipeline model where KV-cache warmup seems to trigger periodic all-reduce stalls. Observed ~12% p99 token latency increase after ~8s into steady traffic.
jonathan: Can you paste the perf counters / nvprof snippets? Which NCCL algo/proto were you on for the run?
samir: Also, what channel count? Channel skew has bitten us before for uneven work distribution.
aya: Test details: dev cluster, 8xA100, model split TP=2 PP=4. Default NCCL settings (algo=ring, proto=LL). Quick nvprof excerpt:
```
[rank0] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 12ms
[rank0] matmul kernel kv_apply 48ms
[rank1..7] small kernels 6-10ms
[nccl] allreduce wait 30-60ms during warmup windows
```
samir: That looks like rank0 compute hot-spot during KV apply. If rank0 runs heavy matmul while others are light, the collective will wait — classic imbalance.
ci-bot: perf-alert: commit 3c4b2ef increased nccl proto fallback rate by +9% on canary.
lina: Could be layered: kernel selection chooses a high-occupancy matmul for kv_apply on rank0 (better throughput single-rank) but harms overlap. Maybe choose a lower-occupancy kernel there to reduce peak time.
jonathan: @aya can you attach the nvtx timeline? Need to see exact overlap between memcpy/matmul/allreduce.
aya: Pasted a trimmed nvtx timeline:
```
Time: 0ms   memcpy_async(rank0)
Time: 12ms  kv_warmup(rank0)
Time: 60ms  matmul(kv_apply)
Time: 108ms nccl:allreduce_start
Time: 140ms nccl:allreduce_end
Other ranks: memcpy_async -> small_fwd -> idle until allreduce_start
```
samir: Thanks. Two immediate hypotheses: (A) kernel selection causing compute skew, (B) KV prefetch happens in a tight burst (all prefetch at same micro-batch), creating synchronized hotspots.
lina: Quick mitigation to test: force proto=LL128 + try algo=tree and increase channels to 4 to reduce ring pressure and improve small-collective latency. Also add kernel-selector hint for kv_apply to pick a "low-peak" matmul.
aya: I ran proto=LL128 + algo=tree + channels=4: p50 unchanged, p99 improved ~7% but we still see spikes aligned with KV miss windows.
jonathan: OK. Proposed parallel experiments: 1) smoothing prefetch across micro-batches (spread KV fetches over 4 micro-batches) to avoid synchronized load, 2) NCCL channel affinity rebalance to move hot ranks across channels, and 3) kernel selection change as lina suggested. We should run combinations.
samir: Also add a synthetic regression test in CI that simulates KV miss bursts and measures p99 with proto variations. If we can detect regressions early we avoid surprises.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary started: 1951234567-ll128-prefetch-smooth (proto=LL128, channels=4, prefetch-smoothing=on)
aya: I'll run the canary tonight on dev-gpu-8 and post the perf summary. If smoothing + LL128 + kernel-hint reduces tail we can roll to canary in prod.
lina: If that works, follow-up: expose a runtime knob for kv_prefetch_spread and default proto=LL128 for small collective workloads.
jonathan: I'll open an experiment PR with scripts to reproduce the trace and a perf dashboard entry.
aya: Thanks — filing notes in perf board and will update with metrics. :thumbsup:
